newsitem.title: USA: Detection Systems CEO sees 97 EPS at $0.70.
newsitem.headline: Detection Systems CEO sees 97 EPS at $0.70.

text.p: Detection Systems Inc Chief Executive Karl Kostusiak said on Wednesday his security-device company would readily meet or exceed a forecast of fiscal year 1997 share profits of $0.70 and $0.99 a share in the next fiscal year ending in March 1998.
The company earned $0.52 in the first nine months of its fiscal 1997 ending this month and last year reported a share loss of $1.83.
Referring to a Raymond James & Associates forecast that his company would earn $0.70 for the full current fiscal year, Kostusiak said, "We're extremely comfortable with that."
Raymond James, sponsor of an investors conference here, which included a speech by Kostusiak, is forecasting Detection Systems's share profits to rise $0.29 in the next fiscal year.
"The estimate of $0.99 for the year that begins in April - we're also very comfortable with that," Kostusiak said.

The brokerage also forecast that Detection Systems will post FY 1997 revenues of $101 million, a figure Kostusiak said was within easy reach. Last year's revenues, before an acquisiton of another security-device group, was $41.9 million.
